findings.title: Age authorization and production now are caller-controlled
findings.evidence: Entry state has no persisted registered_at/not_before fields; Store only parses those values from authorization JSON and accepts the CLI --now. A private fixture retired an entry with caller-supplied 2099 timestamps and 2099 now, while the real entry contained no persisted age field.
findings.impact: A caller can self-assert that a young entry is old enough, and the production route can pass a future --now to defeat age checks.
findings.required_fix: Derive age/not-before from authenticated Store state or a Store-issued audit bound to persisted state; make deterministic time fixture-only and reject caller-controlled production clock overrides.

findings.title: Reference and KEEP/ACTIVE authorization fields are self-asserted
findings.evidence: worker_refs, queue_refs, registration_refs, suite_refs, keep, and active are accepted only as caller JSON values. The implementation requires reference lists to be empty and booleans false, but has no actual worker/queue/service audit and no persisted KEEP/ACTIVE state. It derives only the Store index registrations/suite projections after accepting the caller claims.
findings.impact: A fabricated authorization can claim no live external consumer and inactive state; the required actual-audit boundary is absent.
findings.required_fix: Have Store-owned lifecycle audits derive every reference and state from live registries/leases/markers, bind the audit to the current Store generation, and refuse when any required audit source is unavailable. Do not treat caller lists/booleans as evidence.

findings.title: Process-reference audit has a deletion race
findings.evidence: The final /proc audit returns before journal creation and deletion, with no guard preventing a process from acquiring cwd/fd/cmdline reference afterward. A private fixture started a process in the entry directory after the second audit returned; retirement still returned retired and deleted the directory.
findings.impact: A live process reference can appear between the audit and destructive deletion, violating the concurrent guard requirement.
findings.required_fix: Use an authenticated lifecycle/lease guard that closes the admission race for new process references, or refuse unless the existing lifecycle can provide such a guard; a second scan alone is insufficient.

findings.title: Corrupt retirement receipts are accepted
findings.evidence: _validate_index checks only receipt key-set, derived entry/key/owner identity, and that registrations/suites are lists. It accepts arbitrary path, node, lock, seq, and list element values. A private fixture injected path=7, node=null, lock='corrupt', seq='not-an-int', and suites=[null]; Store.registered() still accepted the index.
findings.impact: Corrupted evidence can be treated as valid Store state instead of failing closed, weakening receipt/recovery integrity.
findings.required_fix: Validate receipt field types and exact ownership/path/inode/lease relationships, list element schemas, uniqueness, and consistency with retirement history; refuse malformed or unreadable receipts.

controls.private_process_race: FAIL: live cwd process raced deletion
